item.title: GM Paying $220 Million to Settle Allegations It Violated Driver Privacy
item.description: General Motors will pay $220 million to settle allegations that it illegally sold drivers’ private behavior and location data to brokers, who then sold the information to insurers that used it to set and sometimes increase rates. The settlement follows GM’s agreement in May to pay $12.75 million to settle a California investigation into its alleged sale of driver data to two data brokers. GM was accused of pitching Smart Driver to help people improve their personal driving safety, only to violate drivers’ privacy by reneging on its promise not to sell their data without permission.

item.title: South Korean Court Rejects Tesla Owners’ Lawsuit Seeking ‘Full Self-Driving’ Refunds
item.description: A South Korean court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by dozens of Tesla owners seeking full refunds for money paid for “Full Self-Driving” driver-assistance software, ruling that the automaker had not breached its contractual obligations. In the lawsuit filed in 2024, the owners said: “Tesla Korea has been unable to implement the FSD system option in South Korea for more than eight years since it began selling it around March 2017.” The plaintiffs argued that Tesla had failed to deliver the promised technology, but the court rejected their interpretation of FSD as a system capable of fully autonomous driving, known as Level 5 automation. In China, 10 Tesla car owners have filed a joint lawsuit demanding refunds for FSD and seeking damages equal to three times the purchase price of the FSD option or the entire vehicle, according to a report.

item.title: Toast Sued by FTC For Misleading Customers on Subscriptions
item.description: Federal Trade Commission and a group of eight states sued Toast Inc., alleging the restaurant management and financial technology company falsely told customers they could try its products for free before enrolling them in a subscription that was difficult to cancel. Toast, which had 156,000 customers and $6.1 billion in revenue last year, violated federal and state consumer protection laws, according to the suit filed Thursday in California federal court. In a statement, Toast said it will fight the suit, arguing the FTC improperly used a 2010 law governing certain online subscription practices to target the company’s commercial agreements with restaurant customers.

item.title: Brits nearly twice as likely to spot pressure tactics in horror films as investment red flags
item.description: Investors are almost twice as likely to recognise pressure tactics in a horror film as they are when those tactics are used to promote an investment opportunity, new FCA data suggests. Lucy Castledine, director of consumer investments at the FCA, said : 'Many people can spot a horror movie trap a mile off, but this survey suggests they’re far less likely to recognise the same tactics when they're used to influence investment decisions. But when faced with a ‘last chance to buy’ investment opportunity, only 36% said it would make them more cautious, while 37% said they would feel pressure to buy quickly or risk missing out.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Travel Tech Funding Heads Toward Multiyear Low Despite AI Push
item.description: The numbers: In the first three quarters of 2026, startups in the travel tech space have raised $2.2 billion globally across just 302 funding rounds, Crunchbase data shows. Travel demand appears to be holding up, but at the same time, investor appetite for travel tech startups has cooled. Even a wave of startups promising to improve travel with AI hasn’t managed to reverse the funding slowdown, a review of Crunchbase data shows.

item.title: The Hartford returns with $280m target for Foundation Re IV 2027-1 cat bond
item.description: The Hartford, a US primary property and casualty insurer, has returned to the catastrophe bond market with an initial target to secure $280 million or more in multi-peril collateralized catastrophe reinsurance protection from the capital markets through sponsorship of a Foundation Re IV Ltd. This latest catastrophe bond from The Hartford will become the eighth transaction is has sponsored since it brought to market the first in the Foundation Re cat bond series of deals back in 2004. Before turning to the new cat bond, the Hartford has $200 million of multi-peril catastrophe reinsurance from the Foundation Re IV 2023-1 issuance that matures around the end of 2026, so it’s good to see this new offering starting at a larger size.

item.title: SCOR sees competition from broker facilities, third-party capital as opportunity: CEO Léger
item.description: I think that SCOR has very good cards to continue to write profitable business in the year to come.” During the call, Léger was asked for his views on broker-led reinsurance facilities in the market, which the CEO linked together with third-party capital and explained that it’s not necessarily all bad for the reinsurers. Thierry Léger, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of global reinsurance firm SCOR, explained this morning that while the market is more competitive, with a proliferation of new capital entering, he sees this as an opportunity for the company, while suggesting that if there are better ways to match risk and capital they should be exploited. Our tier one franchise technical expertise across P&C and life and health, and our strategic capital allocation to diversifying and profitable lines of business position us well ahead of the next strategic cycle and to navigate market headwinds.” Later during the call he was asked about how competition shows up in SCOR’s results, on which Léger acknowledged the inevitability that effects will be seen over-time.

item.title: Tokio Marine HCC International and Adrian Flux develop specialist insurance for domestic humanoid robots
item.description: Tokio Marine HCC International (TMHCCI), part of the Tokio Marine HCC group of insurance companies headquartered in Houston, Texas, has joined forces with UK insurance broker Adrian Flux to introduce a specialist household insurance policy for domestic humanoid robots. Like the driverless car policy we launched in 2016, it will be updated as the technology and the risks evolve.” According to Tokio Marine HCC International and Adrian Flux, the policy is believed to be the first worldwide to combine protection for a domestic humanoid robot with cover for the home in which it operates. Tokio Marine HCC International and Adrian Flux say the product has been developed in response to anticipated demand as domestic robotics becomes more widely available.

item.description: Corgi, an AI-native insurance carrier and financial infrastructure company, has announced the appointment of Morgan Bevin as VP, Public Affairs Officer. Jeremy Eisemann, Chief External Affairs Officer and Deputy General Counsel at Corgi, said: “We’re excited to have Morgan join Corgi as we continue to grow our business and expand our presence across the insurance industry.

item.title: Binance Estimates $6.3 Billion Hacked in Crypto’s Biggest-Ever Heist
item.description: Crypto exchange Binance has suffered a $6.3 billion hack, the largest to hit the digital-asset industry and the latest in a slew of security incidents afflicting the financial sector. Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion in tokens. Binance said in a post on X that about $3 billion of the assets had been frozen on blockchain networks.

item.title: HSBC Seeks to Hedge Data Center Debt With Credit Risk Insurance
item.description: HSBC Holdings Plc is looking to offload credit risk on data center loans to insurers as demand for artificial intelligence-related finance continues to grow. Barclays Plc is looking for insurance on more than $10 billion of AI-infrastructure credit, while Deutsche Bank AG has been working on an SRT tied to about $2 billion in project finance debt, including data center loans. Credit risk insurance, like significant risk transfers, allows banks to mitigate losses and free up regulatory capital that can be used to bid for more business.

item.title: Japan’s Cyberattack Surge Tests Its Push to Strengthen Defenses
item.description: Japan is facing an intense wave of AI-powered cyberattacks that’s laid bare the vulnerability of one of the world’s largest economies to a new breed of hacking. The wave of cyberattacks comes with high stakes because Japan’s industrial conglomerates are key links in the global technology supply chain and the country boasts the world’s second-largest savings pool, all of which are attractive targets for hackers. The crisis is also forcing Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to accelerate plans to bring Japan’s cybersecurity up to the levels of its peers, part of her agenda of making the nation more resilient to external threats.

item.title: AIA Group reports Q3 2026 VONB of US$1,415m
item.description: AIA Group has reported value of new business (VONB) of US$1,415m for the third quarter of 2026, down 5% at constant exchange rates against exceptionally high prior-year comparatives in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland. Lee Yuan Siong, AIA's Group Chief Executive and President, said: "AIA delivered VONB growth of 5 per cent for the first nine months of 2026, despite exceptionally high prior-year sales in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland that affected third-quarter growth. VONB from the Group's other reportable segments outside Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland rose 18%.

item.title: SCOR reports Q3 2026 net income of €206m
item.description: SCOR has reported third-quarter 2026 net income of €206m, down 4.8% from €217m a year earlier, bringing its nine-month net income to €603m. SCOR's Board of Directors met on 29 October 2026, chaired by Fabrice Brégier, to approve the Q3 2026 financial statements. With a solvency ratio of 221%, SCOR is entering the final stretch of Forward 2026 with a strengthened balance sheet as it prepares to unveil its new strategic plan on 3 December." SCOR will unveil its new strategic plan on 3 December, as its Forward 2026 plan comes to an end.

item.title: MS Amlin launches AI wordings tool Wordy Bot for reinsurance contracts
item.description: MS Amlin has launched an AI-powered wordings tool, known internally as Wordy Bot, that analyses reinsurance contracts against its underwriting standards. Wordy Bot identifies missing clauses, wording differences, and potential inconsistencies for review by MS Amlin's underwriters and Wordings team. The tool is already deployed for MS Amlin's North American Property reinsurance book and will support the team during the 1 January renewal season.

item.title: Opterrix Launches AI-Powered Portfolio Management Workflow
item.description: Opterrix (Madison, Wis.) has launched Opterrix Portfolio Management, an AI-powered workflow designed to help P&C insurers analyze portfolio exposures and make underwriting and portfolio-management decisions from a single environment. Opterrix says users can watch the Portfolio Agent run an analysis and take over the workflow at any point. “We want to make that process easier, so insurers can spend less time wrangling data and more time understanding portfolio risk in variable market conditions.” Opterrix Portfolio Management also draws on the company’s existing weather and hazard intelligence capabilities to support event response and ongoing portfolio monitoring.

item.title: Avante Raises $30M to Expand AI Platform for Benefits Teams
item.description: Avante (Seattle) has raised $30 million in Series A funding to expand its AI platform for corporate benefits teams, bringing total funding to $40 million. Avante says the funding will support global expansion and further development of AI agents that help benefits teams analyze programs, evaluate vendors and complete recurring work. “Benefits teams are responsible for one of the largest and most consequential investments their companies make, yet they’re still operating with outdated information, archaic spreadsheets, and technology built for another era,” comments Rohan D’Souza, CEO and Co-Founder, Avante.

item.title: Insurity Dorado Release Expands Rating, AI Risk Intelligence
item.description: Insurity (Hartford, Conn.) has introduced its Dorado release, adding new capabilities across rating, regulatory content management, AI-powered risk analysis and core insurance workflows. Insurity positions Dorado as a practical release focused on helping insurers reduce operational effort while accelerating product changes and improving risk decision-making across the P&C lifecycle. “From rating complex commercial policies in seconds to putting AI-powered insights directly into the hands of decision makers, Dorado reflects our commitment to helping insurers move at the speed of their ambitions.” Dorado also extends AI capabilities within SpatialKey, including natural-language analysis and broader access to geospatial risk information for business users.

Aon’s Global Catastrophe Recap: Third Quarter of 2026 shows insured losses at 3% above the 21st-century average of $88 billion, but they were well below the $135 billion average for the previous five years. accounted for $56 billion in total insured catastrophe losses, with SCSs generating more than $43 billion.

item.title: California Braces for Floods as Atmospheric River Threatens
item.description: California is bracing for flooding as a so-called atmospheric river delivers a glancing blow to the south of the state, before moving across northern Mexico into the U.S. The forecast shows California will be spared a direct hit from the atmospheric river set to arrive in the next few days, the Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes said. The biggest part of the event looks to be Sunday.” Atmospheric rivers are long plumes of moisture traveling thousands of miles across the Pacific and bringing as much water with them as passes through the mouth of the Mississippi River, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

item.title: Probe Outlines Fault in Last Year’s Deadly Hong Kong Residential Tower Blaze
item.description: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologized on Thursday for the deadly blaze that killed 168 people in the city last November, as he released an independent report that held four government departments partially responsible for a fire that erupted after more than a year of safety complaints. “The Committee finds that no Government department took effective ownership of various fire safety issues and complaints about fire hazards fell into a vacuum.” The blaze ripped through seven 31-story tower blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential complex, which was undergoing renovation work in the northern Tai Po district and shrouded in dust netting and scaffolding. “On behalf of the SAR government, I offer my apologies to the victims and the public at large.” Lee also announced the resignation of Hong Kong’s Housing Secretary Winnie Ho — the first official to resign over the inferno.

item.title: Automation Helps Claims Teams Handle Surges
item.description: Hurricane Isaias shows how quickly claims surge after quiet periods, straining leaner teams to review complex restoration invoices thoroughly. For property claims teams, the workload extends well beyond the initial wave of reported losses. While AM Best expects it to be an earnings event for insurers rather than a capital event, the storm created a substantial uptick in work for claims and restoration teams.

For insurance brokers, Ravical compares coverage with changes in a client’s business, including new assets and operational shifts, to flag potential coverage gaps ahead of renewals.

The conspiracy also involved the theft of nineteen premium Husqvarna motorcycles from a Pennsylvania dealership and transportation of the stolen dirt bikes from Massachusetts into Rhode Island. Onix Eduardo was one of four Rhode Island men that were charged for their involvement in a scheme to steal millions of dollars’ worth of high-end vehicles from automobile and motorcycle dealerships across Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Connecticut, and Pennsylvania, according to an announcement after their arrests in 2024 by United States Attorney Zachary A.

item.description: For those of us responsible for crisis preparedness, this presents a real challenge. item.title: FCA encourages former Verus Financial Services Limited customers to check if they can claim with FSCS
item.description: If you were a customer of Verus Financial Services Limited, you can now check to see if you can claim for compensation on the FSCS website . Compensation may be available to former Verus customers through the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), subject to assessment. The FCA is supporting the FSCS as it assesses claims against Verus Financial Services Limited and decides whether individual claims are eligible for compensation.

item.title: California Earthquake Authority seeks $600m reinsurance with Ursa Re 2026-1 cat bond
item.description: The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) has returned to the catastrophe bond market for its second sponsorship of this year, with an initial target to secure $600 million of fully-collateralized earthquake reinsurance from a new Ursa Re Ltd. This new Ursa Re 2026-1 cat bond will become the 25th visit to the market we have tracked by the California Earthquake Authority (CEA). In 2025, the California Earthquake Authority (CEA) sponsored issuance of three series of catastrophe bonds, securing $1.57 billion of earthquake reinsurance protection from the cat bond market.

item.title: Global insured natural catastrophe losses reach $91bn in 9M’26, lowest since 2019: Aon
item.description: According to insurance and reinsurance broker Aon, global insured losses from natural catastrophe events reached $91 billion during the first nine-months of 2026, the lowest for the period since 2019’s $76 billion, and remained well below the $135 billion average of the past five years, but slightly above the 21st-century average of $88 billion. The broker’s latest Global Catastrophe Recap revealed that natural catastrophe losses paid by the global insurance and reinsurance industry in the third-quarter of 2026 reached $29 billion, which Aon said was 31% below the 21st-century average. Economic losses from natural catastrophes in the first nine months of 2026 reached $204 billion, 31% below the 21st century average and marked the lowest first-nine-month total since 2015, Aon further explained.

item.title: Nephila’s multi-year efforts driving higher ILS revenues: Markel’s Crowley
item.description: Nephila Capital, the specialist ILS manager, delivered high revenues and profitability during the third-quarter of 2026 for parent company Markel Group’s financial segment, signifying another step forward in a multi-year effort to develop innovative risk transfer solutions that match investor demand, according to Andrew Crowley, Co-President of Markel Group. In the first nine months of 2026, Nephila Capital has managed to generate $120.3 million in ILS fund management revenues for its parent company Markel, a nearly 42% increase year-on-year compared to the $85 million generated by the end of September 2025. As we reported this morning, Nephila Capital’s insurance-linked securities (ILS) fund management business continues to perform well throughout 2026, as revenues reported within parent Markel’s Q3 2026 results showed an increase of nearly 40% to $42.2 million for the period.

item.title: Radian Group reshapes executive leadership to support strategic growth
item.description: Radian Group Inc., a US financial services company operating in mortgage insurance and specialty insurance, has announced several changes to its executive leadership team. Kobell will also work alongside the executive team to ensure investment decisions align with its strategic objectives, support sustainable business development and deliver long-term returns for shareholders. The appointments are intended to strengthen oversight across its businesses, advance strategic priorities and support sustainable expansion while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk and capital management.

item.title: Hippo’s GWP rises 60% for Q3’26
item.description: Hippo, a technology-native insurance group, has reported an increase of 60.1% in gross written premiums (GWP) to $498 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $311.2 million in the comparative quarter. Hippo explained that its overall growth strategy is focused on improving underwriting profitability and reducing volatility through greater portfolio diversification. The growth lagged, with Hippo explaining that the fast-growing lines, casualty and CMP, are also the lines with the lowest retention levels.

item.title: AXA XL Re GWP & other revenues down 9% in 9M’26 on lower volumes
item.description: During the first nine months of 2026, AXA XL Re saw pricing down -5%, and opted to shrink its book in the period by €200 million which the company says is a reflection of “lower volumes, consistent with our focus on maintaining profitability in a softer market environment.” AXA XL Re forms part of AXA Group’s property & casualty operation, AXA XL, which witnessed a 3% increase in gross written premiums and other revenues during the period to €48.1 billion. As well as the decline at AXA XL Re, AXA XL Insurance, which is part of the commercial lines business, recorded a 1% decline, reflecting disciplined cycle management in a softening market environment with pricing down -1%, and with higher volumes in property and lower volumes in casualty. AXA XL Reinsurance, the global property, casualty, and specialty reinsurance division of AXA Group, recorded a 9% year-on-year decrease in gross written premiums and other revenues during the first nine months of 2026 to €2.2 billion, with the firm pointing to discipline in the softening market.

item.title: Screwworm Reaches Arizona for First Time as Outbreak Spreads
item.description: New World screwworm was found in Arizona for the first time, as cases of the deadly parasite threatening the US cattle herd spread west into a third state. A local veterinarian examined the animal earlier this week and found a wound “heavily infested” with maggots consistent with the New World screwworm, according to the Arizona Department of Agriculture . There have been a total of 71 cases of screwworm in the US since the outbreak began, according to the USDA.

item.title: Midwest Gasoline Supplies Hit Lowest On Record As Election Nears
item.description: Commercial gasoline supplies declined to 41 million barrels — the lowest on record — after falling by 1.2 million barrels last week, according to US Department of Energy data released Wednesday. Gasoline stockpiles in the Midwest have fallen to an all-time low, raising the threat of persistently high pump prices in the region just days away from a handful of crucial Senate elections. Retail pump prices in the Great Lakes recently soared after a surge in wholesale gasoline blendstock prices in Chicago, the regional benchmark.

item.title: Rainier Partners Acquires Texas MGA Platform Apex
item.description: Rainier Partners, a private equity firm investing in lower middle-market services businesses, has acquired Apex Insurance Services, a multi-brand managing general agency (MGA) platform focused on the Texas non-standard auto insurance market. With Rainier’s partnership, Apex plans to continue its organic growth in Texas and potentially new states. Headquartered in Richardson, Texas, Apex manages five MGAs — Apollo MGA, Apollo Specialty, Newstar General Agency, Excellent Insurance Services, and Ignition Insurance Services — creating one of the largest non-standard auto insurance distribution networks in the state.

item.title: Rainier Partners invests in Texas MGA platform Apex Insurance Services
item.description: Rainier Partners, a Seattle-based private equity firm that invests in lower middle-market services businesses, has announced an investment in Apex Insurance Services, a multi-brand managing general agency (MGA) platform focused on the Texas non-standard auto insurance market. "We’ve built an enduring and diversified insurance platform at Apex, and we see significant runway for further expansion in the state of Texas and beyond," said Bryan Ward, CEO of Apex Insurance Services. "Rainier’s experience in our industry, as well as their compatible team culture and roll-up-your-sleeves approach to partnership, made us confident they were the right partners for Apex’s next stage of growth." Jon Altman, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Rainier Partners, said: "Apex is a proven and well-positioned MGA platform that fits squarely within Rainier’s financial services focus, with a strong track record of growth, an experienced and professional team, and impressive reinsurance and retail agent partnerships." Apex is led by a management team with over 100 years of combined experience, and the company says it relies on disciplined underwriting, data-driven pricing, and a broad independent agent network.

item.title: WTW reports Q3 2026 revenue of $2.46bn and 4% organic growth
item.description: WTW has reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $2.46bn, up 8% from $2.29bn in the prior-year quarter, with organic revenue growth of 4%. Risk & Broking revenue was $1,087m, up 8%, with organic growth of 5% and an operating margin of 19.8%. Health, Wealth & Career revenue was $1,350m, up 7%, with organic growth of 4%.
